reviews.text: Robert Eggers’s rousing new film has all the ingredients you’d anticipate in any self-respecting Nordic epic.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Epic, brutally violent, nuanced, and dreamlike, The Northman is a showcase for a unique directorial voice worth celebrating.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Neither tragedy nor Eggers skimp on violence, screams, sweat, blood and swords, along with ambitious mise en scène, some of the best photography and one of the most epic soundtracks of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Medina

reviews.text: Filled with stunning cinematography, the film is an intense, immersive, sometimes surreal, descent into an otherworldly milieu of folkloric horror and medieval barbarism.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: As a bloody and most certainly trippy revenge tale, The Northman is astounding in many places. Eggers may not have created the ultimate Viking tale, but he has crafted an astonishing spectacle that combines his established style with something larger.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Eggers’ visual style is a roller coaster of primordial, oneiric imagery of an epic, wild landscape, turbulent supernatural forces and untamed nature sans any whiff of domestication.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Robert Eggers has crafted one for the ages… The Northman  is a cinematic epic that blew my mind from start to finish. Lavishing cinematography that brings to life this era, visceral violence that adds to the world, & a jaw dropping third act
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The Northman is an incredibly gifted film full of hostility, genealogy, strength, and desire.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Violent and powerful from start to finish, The Northman tells an epic, period accurate Viking tale that easily immerses its audience throughout the entire run-time.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: The Northman is a story that’s been told many times over, and save for showcasing the stunning scenery of Ireland, this adaptation is nothing to write home about.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: The Northman isn’t trying to elevate horror nor dismantle fetishistic fantasies. It’s a fully-formed exercise in realigning blockbuster pictures back to the way they should be: big, visually breathtaking, and bolstered by a unique vision.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: By the time the end credits hit, you will be waiting for it to begin anew, and that is one of the highest compliments you could give a movie of this size and breadth.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: It provides all the weirdness, gore, beauty and singularity that you would expect from this director’s take on a Viking tale of vengeance.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: The Northman’s carefully choreographed, single-shot takes and startlingly lit close-ups blow the spatially disorienting and over-edited style of so many contemporary action films completely out of the fjord.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: The Northman is practically bursting with testosterone. The story of Amleth (Alexander Skarsgård), a Viking Prince hellbent on revenge, Robert Eggers‘s third film is essentially a case study in the destructive nature of unyielding masculinity.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: Northman is one of Robert Egger best films. The scope, the scale, the atmospheric building of Norse mythology is groundbreaking. Along with some insanely well acted performances and beyond thrilling action and revenge based story. Must Watch Masterpiece!
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: The Northman creates a unique saga that taps into something truly primal before one hell of an ending.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Spectacle, pageantry and myth combine with blood, mud and abs for a dazzling, uproarious Viking spree in which Alexander Skarsgård seeks to avenge the murder of his father with the aid of Anya Taylor-Joy and Icelandic national treasure Björk.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: The Northman stands as a stark reminder that there is still a place in cinema for gorgeous, inspired odysseys, rife with literary allusions, deep-seated spiritual meanings, and an exploration of complex human emotions.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: This brutally violent, yet soaringly lyrical action epic is quite unlike anything captured on screen before.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The Northman is an epic the likes of which we hardly see in Hollywood anymore, carefully curated by a master of the medium and packed with powerhouse performances.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Eggers is still a major reason to stay interested in whatever movies are becoming.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Not since Christopher Nolan’s Inception has a studio executive shown such balls of steel, or perhaps I should say boller av stal.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Eggers embraces the filth, the mud, the moss, the viscera that were part and parcel of the day.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: [Eggers has] gone for broke with this epic arthouse blockbuster that mixes Hamlet and Gladiator through the lens of a hardcore metal album cover.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: It is disappointing that The Northman goes past what would have been a truly radical ending and extends itself for a zany climax that qualifies as Valhalla porn.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: The Northman is a brutal and violent film, felt in both its protagonist’s appetite for revenge and a world that seems to require suffering to continue turning.
reviews.author: Erin Schwartz

reviews.text: The Northman isn’t exactly a triumph, but with its many knockout moments, it represents a big step forward for the youngish director Robert Eggers, who for the first time has a big budget ($90 million) to work with.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Hopefully it will be received by audiences for what I believe it is: a memorable, harrowing, cautionary nightmare.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: "The Northman" is winningly engaging at every turn and is best when it becomes an unabashed technical marvel. If it lacks the unpredictable looseness of “The Lighthouse” (Eggers’ best film) it offers clarity of vision with propulsive energy throughout.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: A breathtaking cinematic onslaught that savvily turns hellishness into movie heaven.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A new oddity in which horror, revenge and Norse mythology go hand in hand in one of the most suggestive and visceral shows that we've been able to enjoy on the big screen in the last years.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: A ferocious revenge tale that's heavy on the blood and sweat but light on the tears.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The most violent film I’ve ever seen to also feature a stellar fart joke.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Gratuitously extenuating retina trips... A nightmare in its own right that portrays the tragedy and the end of a treacherous and ultra-masculinized world. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Beastly warriors, assassinated kings, and soothsaying seers look down upon a brutal landscape where the common person could be free one moment and conquered the next with little to say in how their fate will play out... it's best to be prepared for both.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: While The Northman isn't, in the end, as wholly perfect as Eggers debut The VVitch, he's still three-for-three and more ambitious each time he gets behind the camera.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: You can tell Eggers wanted a more elevated, visually-driven movie and I hope a director’s cut shows up someday.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Made me watch The Princess Bride. It's not a coincidence. Like The Northman, it's about vengeance, duels, fights, colorful characters, a love story that destiny couldn't break... I go to bed thinking about it. Not The Northman. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Bobby Eggs might finally be starting to make movies that I can enjoy.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Director and co-writer Robert Eggers is fascinated by the sounds and textures of the pagan and the primal.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The Northman is an exceptionally crafted film with unconventional visuals and a filmmaking voice behind it that is powerfully unique.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Blood runs, mud flies and bones crack — in crisp, percussive ways you’ve hopefully never heard in real life — throughout The Northman, a grand, gut-spilling Norse epic that feels at once earthily ancient and thrillingly modern.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: An authentic-looking and dream-filled world of a thousand years ago, sometimes beautiful and often brutal — but always fascinating.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A savage and mesmerizing Viking saga like no other, Robert Eggers’ The Northman leaves your senses bludgeoned by the time the credits roll.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: A complete cinematic experience from the sound, score, acting, aesthetic, story, and directing is masterfully put together and executed.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: If you’re looking for a bold and nihilistic tale, you’ve come to – quite literally – the perfect place.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: It's brutal and violent, but there's something really beautiful about it.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: A magnificent Mise-en-scène, straddling the subtle and the brutally direct, in a narrative that fearlessly advances towards existential fatalism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Nicole Kidman steals her scenes in this immaculately crafted tale of revenge. The action brings the heat, but the story may leave you cold.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: While the violence, blood, and mud won’t be for everyone, The Northman is a rewarding film for those who venture into its wilderness.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: A historical epic without the epic, a revenge plot with all the agency of revenge removed. What is left?  A two and a half hour plodding viking re-enactment.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: An all-too-rare modern example of an auteur-driven epic, The Northman demands to be seen on the biggest screen possible.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: This is not the sanitized, horned-helmet-wearing, Marvel comics Thor vision of Viking-hood. This is blood and mud and ice and pagan gods, and, reader, I am here for it.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: For all the nonsense The Northman trails in its wake, this is also a big, brawling and absolutely beautifully shot and scored film.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: There is no better word than “visceral”, in its broadest meaning, as a compact synthesis of everything that happens here. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Eggers builds it as a visceral sword-and-sandal epic that never loses its rhythm of action or sense of spectacularity in portraying barbaric times. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: In The Northman, Robert Eggers sheds the title of a horror director. He shows just how far his range can lead him, and it is exciting to see him lean into that.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: It’s not a bad movie in the least, it just feels like a lot of the Eggers special sauce got watered down, even if the brutality went way, way up.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: A Shakespearean nightmare centering on the obsession in which rage reigns supreme, but also its poetry... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: Eggers continues his seemingly meteoric ascent to world-class filmmaker status, expanding his toolkit to encompass a breathtakingly intense, attention-grabbing, single-take approach to scene and story creation unlike anything else.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: It’s a man’s man’s man’s man’s man’s world.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A ferocious, epic tale that is beautifully brutal.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: With its naked sword fight on top of an exploding volcano, The Northman is rad...its blood-soaked tale of vengeance right in line with the great Icelandic sagas, an epic cinematic rendering of a story that has been told for at least a thousand years
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Visually it is darkly stunning, but storywise it is all over the place. Nicole Kidman is one film and Alexander Sharsgard is in another. Anna Taylor-Joy doesn't know where the heck she's supposed to be.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Eggers' film didn't resonate with me after I left the theater. I never felt pulled into the orbit of Amleth's revenge close enough to really empathize with his plight. Gorgeously shot yet oddly hollow emotionally.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: I wanted to love Robert Eggers’s follow-up to The Witch and The Lighthouse, but maybe a big-budget Viking saga just isn’t the right fit for a wonderful weirdo like him?
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text:
An immersive event from its first seconds.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: This is a movie that doesn't shy away from emotions, it embraces them fully. The actors don't shy away from overacting, either, they revel in it, and this is both refreshing and entertaining.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: You genuinely feel how much his characters have faith in their gods and their folk tales as an extension of their everyday lives.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: The Northman is brutal, bloody and violent, even a little gory at times. But its beautiful aesthetics displayed in every shot and every sequence place it above other movies with similar topics. [REVIEW IN SPANISH]
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: Hyper-stylized… form triumphs over substance.
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text:
If we are fools in doubt, we can break the cycle of violence and revenge...or else leave behind a scorched Earth…where only losers can reside.
[Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Epic, massive, and ostentatious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: Eggers' latest is wicked and delightfully weird without ever losing its grip on being a compelling character study engulfed in dazzling imagery. It’s his best film to date and the most confounding studio film of the year.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: ...an epically-misguided trainwreck that couldn’t possibly be less interesting or involving.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: What Eggers has done with this film is to develop an intense story of revenge, without hiding how barbaric and bloody and brutal life was at that time for these people. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The Northman falls short of being an epic film, but the mastery in composition of the film is noteworthy.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Execution, performance, and art direction are all unparalleled, but the whole simply proves a solid familial melodrama in the end. They can’t all be "great."
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Eggers has embraced the wildness. creating a world of primal ritual where the spirit realm regularly interacts with the material one, and life is nasty, brutish, and short. Mercifully so.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Predictable at every turn, but the operatic style of the effects leave you entranced - even chilled - for the entire film
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: This is a film that gives what is wanted, without any regrets, through an environment that’s as angry as it is awesome.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: Drenched in testosterone, Northman is less concerned with reinventing the wheel with it's narrative built on the same mythology that inspired Hamlet, but rather with making you feel the visceral human anger and rage underpinning it's entire proceedings.
reviews.author: Jessie Gender

reviews.text: A death-metal ode to honor, retribution and sacrifice that casts payback in a surprisingly, and thrillingly, positive light.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: It’s a good movie, yet also a little disappointing, because it’s not quite good enough to get away with being so little fun.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: he tale of Amleth (played wonderfully here by Alexander Skarsgård) could be called Shakespearian.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: If meant to be a provocative meditation on freewill and revenge, and a bloody, visceral, painstakingly-detailed spectacle  it maybe only delivers on the spectacle.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: A violent, visceral, and engrossing voyage.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: Exciting and sprawling, The Northman is almost a throwback to an earlier time of movie-making, with a story of redemption, presented in a fascinating and spellbinding way.
reviews.author: Louie Fecou

reviews.text: A brutal, testosterone-fueled profusion of "Game of Thrones", 300, and Kill Bill
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: Both beautiful and brutal, The Northman is a saga worth seeing.
reviews.author: Lee Jutton

reviews.text: Skarsgård never once puffs his chest to assert his place as the hero, in complete alignment with Amleths sense of prophecy bestowed upon him at an early age.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: The storyline was simple yet effective. The landscape, the production values -- I was all in.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Overall, despite the lavish treatment, the film is surprisingly dreary...
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: It's the creative juices of Robert Eggers that gives The Northman its unique identity, from the impeccable detail and design to the wild flourishes and overindulgences.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: As we get to summer with a lot of polished blockbusters, this is something a bit grittier, and a bit more interesting.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: It's Hamlet with a lot more blood and a lot less clothes.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Striking and compelling, for a film that toys with the concept of defying one's fate, the narrative does feel disappointingly stuck to a predetermined path, missing the surprises of Eggers' past films.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: What you’ll get is neither the bold weirdness of Eggers’s previous efforts in the critically-acclaimed margins nor a clean strike into the blockbuster mainstream.
reviews.author: Colleen Morrissey

reviews.text: The Northman is signature Eggers, with an almost maniacal dedication to period authenticity, big themes and some surrealist and supernatural touches.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: "The Northman" is a sweeping epic driven by blood and brutality, offering up a bleak and unrelenting take on the legend that inspired it. It might be great - hell, it almost certainly IS great - but sadly, it left me behind.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: This is teenager cinema par excellence, an opera of old-world mayhem fit for Beavis and Butthead.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Eggers take a predictable revenge tale and makes it his own, especially early on. Definitely a slow-burn that builds effectively with assured, confident direction that also asks for patience. Visually, it's one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: Its better than most of the current movies in its weight class but its less than that of which we know Eggers is capable.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: I would say it's one of my favorite movies of the year, but it's really one of my favorite experiences of the year.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: A rude, bloody, hyper-violent Viking saga like nothing you’ve ever seen.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Through it all, Egger pulls excellent performances from his cast, maintains a steady forceful tone and drives the storylines to a cataclysmic ending. Try as you may, you can’t take your eyes off the screen.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: If anyone is victorious, it's the viewer of this immersive saga, who will emerge wobbly-legged, dazed and probably a little more appreciative of the relative tameness of modern life.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Pure cinematic bliss. Great performances, a blood-soaked revenge story and Karin Blaschke' gorgeous shots - all amazing. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: To prepare for this role, Alexander Skarsgård has bulked up to superhero proportions. A mass of muscle with a weapon in each hand, hes a terrifying prospect.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Robert Eggers has a unique conception for the film, and he's guided his actors and technical team to bring it to the screen with extreme vividness.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Will sure tickle those that have come to expect nothing less from a filmmaker unafraid to be bold and gorgeously weird.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A sweeping tale of laser-focused retribution, woven into the alien tapestry of ancient Nordic myth.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: An incredibly well-made and well-acted film with some spectacular attention to detail, but the slight story and Skarsgard's stoic performance undermines Eggers' technical achievements.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: Eggers recreated, with obsessive accuracy, the world of the medievals in order to lower us into a myth that feels primordial and strange, as if it’s tapping into something in the back of our minds that we’ve always known but half forgotten.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: 'The Northman' may not be your kind of movie. Eggers does not seem to care whether or not the violence offends you. His purpose is to showcase a brutal time when life and death meant less than today.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: With his third feature film The Northman, Robert Eggers delivers brutal violence with gorgeous cinematography that entrances the viewer from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Mary Beth McAndrews

reviews.text: A sublime technical feat with no emotional core. Eggers doesn't offer anything new or subversive to the Hamlet tale, including its discussion on masculinity. Skarsgård feels miscast (or perhaps Anleth is just boring?)
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: It's all very bleak and cruel. And stylistically intoxicating.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Robert Eggers delivers exactly what youd expect from the filmmaker. However unlike his previous projects, THE NORTHMAN may be the most straightforward film, but it still veers into the weird realm.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Where the movie goes south is in its narrative and characters. Beneath the twisting Scandinavian folklore is a simple and familiar revenge story that never gives us real reason to care.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Its easy to get lost in time during those two hours.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: It certainly feels authentic -- there’s a sense of constant otherness to what we experience on the screen, yet with no sense of contrivance -- and that’s what matters. Everything feels strange, savage, implacably other.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: The Northman is a well-realized film full of action and an easy-to-understand story that might not be for everyone.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: The Northman isn’t exactly a triumph, but with its many knockout moments, it represents a big step forward for the youngish director Robert Eggers, who for the first time has a big budget to work with.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The tamest Eggers film yet. Lacking in the depth department, but fantastic looking.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: The Northman is a sight to behold and the work of a director who has cemented his ability to transport audiences into worlds inhabited by the strange
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: Eggers has quickly established himself as an auteur with a specific voice, and The Northman proves that having a bigger budget only enhances his strengths.
reviews.author: Paul Dika

reviews.text: It is a visually stunning, breathlessly violent, bone-crushingly metal take on Viking legend.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text: The Northman doesnt offer anything new narratively, but it may be the most vicious movie to hit cinemas this year and its certainly one of the most beautifully shot.
reviews.author: Kyle Logan

reviews.text: Iceland's hottest new club is "The Northman." Located at the Gates of Hel, this place has everything.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: You never would accuse Robert Eggers of being just another filmmaker.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: "When I was an hour into the film, I thought how Eggers could have just gone ahead and taken on Conan. But by the end, I was pulled into Eggers grander, more complex vision."
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Not unlike parts of Quentin Tarantino's "Inglourious Basterds," "Django Unchained," and the "Kill Bill" opus, the filmmakers build the tension with a nerve-rattling, deliberate pace and often make you think you're seeing something that is merely implied.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: Few mainstream films are allowed to be this bold, combining hallucinatory imagery with visceral action. Eggers tells a Nordic revenge story classic in its accessibility, but fueled with a style that refuses to water down the material.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Genuinely amazing!
reviews.author: Lorry Kikta

reviews.text: The Northman is gripping cinema of the sort that we get too little of today, when too often a director’s vision is diluted by box office imperatives and the lure of four-quadrant appeal.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Savage, supernatural and often silly, Robert Eggers' intense Nordic nightmare is filled with brawling, bloody brutality.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A beautifully bloody empty shell.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: While other, nobler films often treat vengeance as something poisoned and futile, The Northman asks us: what if revenge was a satisfying, orgasmic triumph of sheer nirvana?
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: Realism and mythology converge in this grandiose and brutal visual spectacle that explores a familiar territory in the revenge saga genre. Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: None of the players should be blamed for the uneven historical canvas or the unnecessary length of some scenes. Regardless, if anyone really is looking to be entertained by stories of this ilk, I suggest a 1958 spectacle simply called 'The Vikings.'
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: This visually striking and brutally violent battle epic unspools a visceral exploration of primal instincts and toxic masculinity thats set in the 10th century but still resonates today.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Visually, its absolutely stunning, but the sullen tone of "The Northman" makes it a bleak, one-note opus.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The Northman" offers elaborately staged hatred and death. It was popular then; its popular now.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: "The Northman" follows the breadth of savagery in savage lands. There is no escaping the pall of terror it reveals. Eggers is a master at blending psychology and cinema. He plays mind games with his most assuredly cowering audience
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Visually gargantuan, thrumming with strange noise and even stranger visions, this is not even your grand-daddy's grand-daddy's Shakespeare - this is the bastard child of George Miller's Mad Max Fury Road and Darren Aronofsky's The Fountain
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Theres so much more below the surface that feels almost locked away behind a fortress of sparse dialogue and explanation. The Northman, sadly, isnt as inviting as it needs to be for viewers wanting to explore the world the film presents to them.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: It’s an impressive piece of time travel. Eggers succeeds in conjuring up a world governed exclusively by blood feuds and territorial imperatives. And Skarsgard, who helps initiate the production, makes a magnificently realised Amleth.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Though the film narrowly avoids being a contrived blockbuster, it still is not refined enough to exhibit the kind of storytelling prowess that Eggers is capable of.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: Robert Eggers has established himself as a master of mood and tone since he dragged us by our eyebrows with The VVitch. Here, he’s working with a much broader canvas and a sizable budget, and acquits himself astoundingly well.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: If you are fan of old-school epic tales of revenge, then The Northman is the movie for you. It’s a cinematic throwback that is a step forward for Eggers.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: At nearly two and a half hours, that may be a lot to ask for anyone hoping for a straightforward thriller, but for those willing to get invested, there’s significant treasure in store.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Even though there's actually little going on here outside of a revenge plot, the movie has weight to it, something at stake. It feels like it was crafted by people with pride in their craft.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: That mix of detail-oriented realism and wild swings into mysticism and animalistic combat isn't just a budgetary flex; it lends The Northman a thematic gravity that keeps it from floating off into self-indulgent silliness.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: The Witch, The Lighthouse and The Northman all reflect their director’s penchant for exacting attention to detail and hard-earned madness.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: The Northman is a lot of things—bruising, rousing, and often entertaining—but it’s not particularly complex.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Robert Eggers delivers a bloody good Shakespearean revenge epic.
reviews.author: Alex Nguyen

reviews.text: The Northman is not for the faint of heart. Its a haunting, bold, and brutal Viking epic.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It holds our attention with unforgettable visuals and the sheer, raw audacity of its premise.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Think you know what a Viking is? You have no idea.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: For all its physicality, The Northman (like Eggers’ other tales) hinges on emotion and superstition.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The Northman is an epic saga of revenge...unflinchingly realistic, deliberately paced and leaves you with your breath taken and your mind expanded.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Eggers makes "The Northman" as crafty as an art film, as brutal as a slasher flick - two-plus hours of arthouse savagery.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The Northman might be Eggers at his most traditional, yet its his best feature, which is saying a lot because hes created nothing but bangers. It makes me wanna run to Iceland and grow a beard and abs.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A bloody, muddy, beautiful and sometimes surreal vision of Norse myth.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Represents a successful transition to the higher-budget echelon for its director
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The Northman has a limited payoff after two hours, and not even an unexpected finale saves it from averageness.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Eggers exhumes the bones of a primal myth and arranges them in spectacular fashion, no doubt. But just as The Northman itself is interested in scrying meaning from old ways, you'll want to find something to take away here.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: An intense, brutal, and captivating two-plus hours of watching bad people pay for their past deeds. Yes, revenge is cold, but in "The Northman," it arrives in a top-notch artistic package.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Worth the watch for the intense, authentic period setting and grittygorgeous depiction of a legendary revenge story. Though the film takes itself a bit too seriously. As is often the case, Anya Taylor-Joy is the best thing about it.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Not all of The Northman works -- some of it’s muddled visually and linguistically, and at turns it gets a bit too feral for its own good -- but the immersion and mood makes for a mesmerizing and haunting odyssey.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The Northman, whether you approach it as legitimate folklore or as a testosterone-fueled Saturday-afternoon lark, speaks to the 10-year-old boy in all of us, with a loud and mighty Viking burp.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Fire and brimstone meet rot and decay, yet theres ambition afoot here. Eggers deserves a great deal of the credit for crafting another startling, big screen vision.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Eggers’ miscast, moody, turn-of-the-10th-century action adventure seems late to the Norse feast despite, or perhaps because of, its overserious intentions.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: The film feels oddly flat, mitigated as it is by the cross purposes of its creator and the studio that backed it.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: The Northman envelopes its conventional swords-and-sandals plot with a vibe and aesthetic that is both unhinged and seductive.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: More than a little over the top, this piece of bloody eye candy from ancient Viking life is a tasty, visually intoxicating  guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: “The Northman” is authentic atavistic cinema, a bulletin from the before times fashioned by one of the great natural filmmakers of the present.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Its most notable quality is the way it refuses to bend its characters to the present, preferring instead to make them as alien in their perspective as possible.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Forget fire and ice (though there is that, too); revel instead in arterial spray. What more could you ask for? Its AD 895, and times are tough.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A sensory triumph more than it is an emotional one, this is nonetheless an enthralling endeavor, everything building to a crushing finale of senseless masculine bravado thats as gut-wrenchingly beautiful as it is tragically heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Psychological probing is squashed, like many onscreen skulls. It all leads to a slog of a saga of slaughter.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Lets get to why youre really here: Yes, Willem Dafoe does appear in both a Viking-era dog costume AND in his underpants AND as a disembodied head. Its all true.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Its a rarity in todays IP-saturated cinematic climate that a director like Eggers is permitted to take this wild a swing, and even rarer that their major studio debut feels so of a piece with their earlier works.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: The emotional connection meanders, but the production and Skarsgard's physical performance fly sky-high.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: It offers us almost no quarter, and asks none of us. For that, it has to be respected. Not many big-budget period movies are this unwilling to throw a sop to modern attitudes.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: If youre looking for an unapologetically bloody and masculine movie with just a dash of eerie energy to it, youll probably dig The Northman.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: His attempt to juxtapose ambition with cinematic bloodlust is not always successful, but when it works, the savagery on display can be breathtaking.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: A payback tale for the ages.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Working for the first time with a blockbuster-scaled budget, Eggers can give full range to his feverishly inventive imagination, and the result is often hypnotic...
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Instead of the roots of Shakespeare’s play, “The Northman” merely serves up its raw material both half-baked and overcooked.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Eggers manages to infuse this straightforward tale with plenty of his unique sensibilities.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The Northman goes beyond just being another story about Viking savagery and delivers a film that is steeped in lore, rituals, and prophecies. Its brutal yet beautiful with ferocious action sequences paired with stunning visuals.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: A brutal film made for adults that shows us the maturation of an important cinematic voice.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: For all its relentless fury and fire, "The Northman" has a remote iciness that hampers emotional investment in the Shakespearean heroes and villains. That said, its vast medieval-era storytelling is stunning in its vivid and realistic presentation.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: If you want to see a cinematic spectacle of Viking violence and warrior masculinity - this is going to be for you!
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Director Robert Eggers hot-stamps medieval suffering into a titanic work of art.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Eggers serves up a Viking Hamlet. It wasn't as unhinged as we were hoping for, the plot is echoic, and many characters (particularly the female ones) lacked dimension. There's however justtt enough going for the film for it to have been watchable for us.
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: Its a film that sears itself into the senses via nightmares glimpsed in the hellish half-light.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: The Northman misses the thematic depth of Eggers first two films, but the talent on display is unmistakable and cements Eggers as a force of nature as mercurial and frightening as Amleths rage.
reviews.author: Terry Mesnard

reviews.text: A tumultuous, graphically gorgeous entertainment for our time as well as an ineffably somber meditation on our species’ seemingly inexhaustible reservoir of savagery.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The Northman makes you realize that, perhaps, an entire life grieving what you lost can truly stop you from what you can gain. diandrareviews
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: Alexander Skarsgård slays as a prince dishing out ice-cold vengeance in the musclebound, medieval epic "The Northman."
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: The Northman is an intense, nail biter that is going to leave a lasting mark on the epic period drama. With gorgeous cinematography and phenomenal performances from Skarsgard, Taylor-Joy, and Kidman, this is a film you should see in theaters.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: We rarely get movies like this anymore, with an emerging auteur given the time and money to craft the big-budget film that he wants to make. The fact that The Northman is as good as it is almost feels like a bonus.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Its certainly a spectacle, for all its slower moments, but a largely effective and successful spectacle: by the time the credits roll, its hard not to be utterly swept away by it.
reviews.author: Keri O'Shea

reviews.text: Quite possibly the first truly great movie of 2022. It might even be the first truly great movie we’ve gotten in a couple of years.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Eggers indulges both the grand folklore of the Viking age and the commonplace reality that shaped it, successfully creating an odyssey that feels grounded in the actual demands of civilization.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Eggers does not care if the moviegoing public comes away having learned about themselves or achieved some measure of catharsis. The film serves the internal needs of its protagonist, nothing more. The conceit is admirably single-minded.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Northman, Robert Eggers’ biggest and most expansive (and expensive) feature to date, is also his best so far.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Eggers' commitment to verisimilitude means that he conveys every sweaty, grimy, bloody experience of the characters in vivid detail.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: A visually enthralling evocation of a distant world, blending history and myth in a composite awash in bloodshed and butchery yet strangely intoxicating even in its excesses...Yet dramatically it leaves something to be desired.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Director/co-writer Robert Eggers has sought to make the definitive Viking movie, and while the film issues a guttural cry for theatrical viewing, it is built around such a basic revenge plot as to blunt those simple charms.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Eggers presents misshapen children who grow to be fearsome beasts, these simple tales told through cruelty and magic that resonate regardless of the setting. Eggers is more comfortable shaping and molding folklore and mythologies with dark symbolism.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: For the first time, it feels like Eggers is relying on pagan pageant more than psychology to drive the movie, and the result is a seance that doesn’t quite spellbind, despite a sincere effort to.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: What’s perhaps most impressive about “The Northman” is that it hurtles through 136 minutes of musclebound, shaggy-maned mayhem without a whisper of camp or a wink of irony.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: "Northman" is relentlessly brutal, but the violence feels appropriate for a world in which there aren't any rules and where "social change" comes at the sharpened edge of an ax.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: There is swordplay, soap opera style revenge, surprising nudity, a howling ritual and a fight on an active volcano. But it can be viewed as a blood and guts old fashioned adventure through the filter of Robert Eggers. Why wasn't Nick Cage in this movie?!?
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: A hell of a movie and youre unlikely to see utter weirdness on such a grand scale anywhere else.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: So many movies about Vikings never convince us that we’re watching anything but actors dressed like Vikings. This one’s chanting in Old Norse and Old Ukrainian makes the film far more persuasive.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: It's a brawny, lusty, bloody epic of big emotions and in-your-face intensity, a movie that happens TO you as you're watching it, both visually and aurally.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Hypocrisy is by no means fatal, but despite a glorious climactic duel on a lava-drenched volcano, The Northman leaves weary familiarity in its wake.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The Northman is an excellent, unflinching, and immersive vision from filmmaker Robert Eggers.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: "The Northman" feels like the culmination of Eggers' powers as a writer and director, taking his knack for creating moody atmosphere and his gift for words and staging them on an epic canvas.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: ...made with blistering cinematic vision.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Visually stunning and painstakingly choreographed, The Northman perfectly measures up to its epic expectations.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: With his remarkable attention to folkloric detail, filmmaker Robert Eggers takes on Viking mythology in this bloodthirsty meditation on revenge.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Once ... the underlying ideas about revenge come into sharper focus, the filmmakers don't develop those...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: If this is how we get our big screen Sword & Sorcery revival, with inward seeking filmmakers taking a stab at arguably the most externally pleasurable genre, sign me up.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: The mood, the detail and the look of this production is extraordinary. And the fiery showdown at the end is incomparable.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: A wild and trippy ride, big, mythic, violent, and wonderful. Eggers once again proves that hes not only a filmmaker with his own crazy and specific vision, but that he has the skills to pull it off.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Its a familiar story of payback, violent, visceral and vengeance-filled, but Robert Eggers singular vision, and fondness for ancient symbolism and psychedelia, make it a unique experience.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Hypnotic visuals with a bland story.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: A monumentally bonkers, blood-smeared battering ram of Old World barbarism.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Eggers distinct vision will thrill some, offend others, but ultimately offer an experience you wont soon forget.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Robert Eggers' The Northman is an extraordinary feat of cinema – but it's also a bloody, mournful, violent tale of vengeance that is never simply academic, but visceral, sensual, emotional, and epic.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: As the central revenge plot proved too familiar even from this most distinctive of directors, I found myself only able to appreciate it in terms of its filmmaking craft.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: “The Northman” lavishly rewards fans of the swords-and-vandals genre, even if it leaves the rest of us in bludgeoned, bemused awe.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: “The Northman” fills out its widescreen canvas, carefully and meticulously.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The Northman is an extravagant and unshackled cinematic experience with a vibe akin to a rock opera performed at the foot of an active volcano.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: a deft blend of arthouse flick and historical drama, dripping with atmosphere and anchored by strong performances and superb direction.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: It doesn't just cut to the bone, it tears apart flesh, splatters blood in our faces and spits in our eye.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: More of Olgas strong character & less of the bellicose brutality of the male ones wouldve helped Eggers in his critique of toxic masculinity. Instead, his savaging of machismo is dampened by all the savagery he insists on splattering across the screen.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Sheer fun ride into darkness
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Eggers’s action sequences are swift and brutal, filled with the crunch of life extinguished and tossed into the bone pile of time. Skarsgård, hulking and seething, is a fine vessel for the film’s opulent menace.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Still and all, theres something missing here. While we may understand everyones intention, theres no emotional connection with any of them.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Another killer entry in the filmography of a storyteller who cannot be contained.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: “The Northman” is both a dazzling display of film craft and a sly retooling of genre, a movie that delights in fulfilling certain conventions while turning others on their artfully severed heads.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Equal parts beautiful and desolate like a part of Icelands own volcanic countryside, iThe Northmani is auteur Robert Eggers most straightforward film, making up in style what it gives up in the complexity of his previous films.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: This movie is so visceral you can feel it reverberating inside your body, which is exactly what makes it so delightful.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: An achievement for the helmer, but he's easily distracted here, working tirelessly to manufacture an immersive viewing event, leaving dramatic power limited.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: As unusual and occasionally off-putting as The Lighthouse was, it was but a warning shot for the persistent madness of The Northman, a film designed to maintain a sense of uncanny threat in every frame.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: This is cinematic storytelling at its finest. Drawing from Norse and Icelandic myths, it's also unmistakably Shakespearean in theme. While it's magical, mystical and symbolic, it's not confusing. I admire and appreciate that.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The secret to The Northman's success is simple: it delivers everything you could want from a Viking movie.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Skarsgård has thrown himself into Eggers' latest with full force, and it shows: not only does he look incredible, but he's operating at the absolute peak of his abilities with a performance that will certainly be among the highlights of his career.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Thanks to intensely committed performances, the keen lensing of cinematographer Jarin Blaschke and clear motivations that drive the plot along like a humming V8 engine, The Northman does revenge as well as anyone could.
reviews.author: D. Patrick Rodgers

reviews.text: The Northman is a cinematic experience that could only come from Robert Eggers.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Eggers has solidified his legacy as a wonderful director and there are no doubts, he will be making movies, possibly even Oscar worthy ones, for many years to come.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: An inert bore stricken by leaden direction by Robert Eggers who, despite an obviously huge budget, renders the film with absolutely no sense of adventure or excitement.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The Northman doesn't so much adopt the plot of Hamlet as dig beneath it to unearth the ur-story that predates Shakespeare by centuries. So while the tale's broad strokes are familiar, its particulars can vary in intriguing ways.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: The Northman takes viewers on a magnificent adventure.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: A visually stunning, but vapid, tedious and exhausting video game.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Robert Eggers is a visual master.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: It is melodrama, and murder and mayhem and witchcraft; its everything Robert Eggers does best on the biggest scale, and its his best film yet.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: THE NORTHMAN is how epics should be done.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Around the sturdy mythic pillars of regicide-slash-fratricide and seething vengeance, Eggers and Sjón have fashioned an almost-original creation, a mud-and-gore-slicked work of historical verisimilitude spiked with fly agaric and raging testosterone.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: 'The Northman' is a film that, in relation to subject matter, budget and lack of an IP, should not exist in 2022. Warts and all, it's a miracle of a movie.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Once you settle in for the ride and commit yourself to whatever hellish vision Eggers cultivates, "The Northman" doesn't just subvert expectations, it obliterates them.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Eggers doesnt compromise on the brutality and scale of his latest feature, creating a visually compelling and absorbing thriller. Combined with Skarsgårds powerful performance, The Northman cements a welcome return to the cinematic historical epic.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Gritty, bloody, visceral and front-loaded with a need for vengeance, the latest work from writerdirector Robert Eggers (The Witch, The Lighthouse) is so immersive and authentic, you'll feel the muck between your toes and every blow across your body.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: A guttural, primal grunt of a movie that is all raging testosterone and incendiary machismo. And I loved nearly every minute of it.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: THE NORTHMAN is a wild ride. Its dark, violent, gory and very entertaining.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: At two hours and sixteen minutes, THE NORTHMAN moves quickly. I could not take my eyes off the screen.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: This is a ghastly, grisly, ultra violent film that is hard to watch, but also hard to look away from this visually striking take on ancient Viking lore.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The Northman is well-acted, directed, and undeniably thrilling.  Alexander Skarsgård cuts a swath of bloody vengeance in a ferocious Viking epic. The film vividly combines a Hamlet-esque narrative with Scandinavian history and mythology.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Eggers has what you might call a singular vision. Here, hes made a film that feels like it was beamed directly from the long-dead skull of a Nordic bard.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: It might not be subtle, it might not even be particularly deep, but it sure is spectacular.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: Despite efforts from the Valkyries and Odin’s ravens, this Viking action art piece is fettered to the ground by the demands of the studio gods.
reviews.author: Scott Greenstone

reviews.text: Once again, I can’t quite see what all the excitement is about, as the American director combines a sub-Shakespearean tale of murder and revenge with Viking mythology, shamanistic ritual and a huge amount of bloody Dark Ages violence.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: '...a mighty, nasty-ass epic of treachery, pagan horror and bloody revenge...'
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: 300 meets Midsommar, and probably the most realistic Viking movie to date. Part ancient myth, part Shakespeare, part History Channel. This might not be a "fun" movie but it's a visceral experience worthy of the big screen - and your time.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Robert Eggers' blistering epic 'The Northman' is a raw, bloody, and brutal Viking revenge saga that splatters blood and brilliance on every inch of its canvas.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: The Northmans unrelenting blood-soaked story plays out against a brooding, hostile landscape that Eggers makes full use of.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: It’s as ambitious as it is preposterous and, at times, ponderous – filled with garbled epithets about vengeance and fate that are whispered, muttered, or blood-curdlingly yelled.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The Northman, with its vicious blend of blood and ice, feels like the crowning achievement for one of the most idiosyncratic and unique filmmakers working in Hollywood today.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: A testosterone burst that serves as a visceral and audiovisually stunning psychological study of the toxic macho hero figure... Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Brutally violent but artistically stunning, The Northman brings harsh realism and dreamy mythology to this Viking story that inspired William Shakespeare's Hamlet ... The end result is an immersive cinematic experience that is both menacing and magical.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It is two hours and fifteen minutes of violent, animalistic ritual, a testosterone-fueled orgy of masculinity, a film so dark, dirty, raw, and hardcore it makes The Revenant look like Jane Austen.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Coming as a follow-up to The Witch and The Lighthouse, this 90 million effort packs all of that budget on screen while still holding onto the off-the-wall qualities that make Eggers a standout genre filmmaker.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Director Robert Eggers' blood-soaked Viking epic is equal parts brutal and breathtaking, a truly immersive cinematic experience that makes the almost-140-minute runtime pass in the blink of an eye.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: It’s rather ripe for parodying, though you can’t deny the film’s power and scale as well as the beauty and strangeness of the landscape, in turn green and lush and black and icy.
reviews.author: Markie Robson-Scott

reviews.text: Although neither as moody nor wacky as his first two films, it’s another masterful achievement from one of the English language’s most exciting contemporary arthouse filmmakers.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The Northman is everything we expect from director Robert Eggers  dark, surreal, atmospheric with a poetic intimacy for character building.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Metal as hell! An arthouse 'Conan the Barbarian' that makes 'Game of Thrones' look like 'Snow White'
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: A cinematic wonder of Viking violence and old-school melodramatic barbarity, The Northman is an unrelenting and gruesome historic epic that showcases an absolutely berserk performance from Alexander Skarsgård.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The Northman is magical, mystical and relentlessly masculine, but also, in places, perhaps a little too much.
reviews.author: Laura Stott

reviews.text: For all its virtues The Northman is an unrelentingly bleak spectacle, nobody's idea of a fun night out.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Robert Eggers delivers a masterful film about the power of myths to inform our own lives.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: You can always count on things to get weird with Eggers, but that doesn’t necessarily mean they get interesting.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: “The Northman” is at once overwhelming and curiously uninvolving.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Eggers needs to allow some moments of quiet so we can get to know the characters and feel invested in their journeys. This was too much of everything
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: "Bloody but brilliant medieval vengeance tale."
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: What’s so amazing and essential about The Northman is how populist and accessible it is to any viewer who buys a ticket while Eggers also retains so much of what makes him such a unique and interesting director.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Eggers' take on the Vikings is something to behold and marvel at.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: Eggers is a skilful and imaginative director, and his films achieve almost unbearable levels of intensity: The Northman is a brilliantly realised saga that burrows its way to the heart of the Viking sensibility.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The Northman is one of the most visceral cinematic experiences for some time. A bold, bloody & violent tale of vengeance & fate, its a captivating but trippy journey which wont work for everyone.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Our adoration of The Northman has little to do with the level of violence on screen... and more to do with the craft, scope and skill that went into creating the first great blockbuster of the year.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: The stakes though inviting as they may seem are underwrought. And while that may be their very purpose on the page, in the film the absence of engaging reasons to stay invested undermines the entirety of the saga Eggers seeks to tell.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: One of the most breathtakingly nuts movies in recent years, a died-in-the-wool Viking revenge epic that feels every bit like a visionary has been given money to burn for the first time in his life, and is going to take full advantage of it.
reviews.author: Owen Gabbey

reviews.text: Never compromising his unique style, Eggers crafts a visceral Viking epic with The Northman. Eggerss spellbinding blend of blockbuster and art house gives us a haunting experience that will be celebrated amongst the upper echelon of cinema in 2022.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Praise the Norse gods, for not only is The Northman an exhilarating revenge saga that outdoes most modern blockbusters when it comes to action sequence staging and immersive sound design, but Eggers’ penchant for the strange remains fully intact.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: The director of 'The Witch' made a Norwegian black metal Hamlet starring Alexander Skarsgard as an angry Viking. That's it, that's the review.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The film's extreme violence, ambiguous moral stance and delve into supernatural folklore might alienate certain viewers, but this ranks alongside other great revenge epics such as Gladiator in terms of sheer excitement and spectacle.
reviews.author: Max Copeman

reviews.text: With viciousness relegated to its margins, it often feels neutered and bloodless, but still ends up on the right side of entertaining thanks to its pulsating music and measured performances.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The beauty of this film isnt the story but the visual feast for the eyes, the direction, cinematography, editing and the world created by the co-writer and director, Robert Eggers.
reviews.author: Rosalynn Try-Hane

reviews.text: As I think about it, this Hamlet-clone needs something more, like a heart and soul. "The Northman" has neither. Brutal battles alone do not make an epic. It takes a good story, too.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Eggers commitment to maintaining period accuracy and influences makes for a visual feast but binds it narratively. The mesmerizing style and mysticism ensure its deeply engrossing.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: Eggers treats the big screen reverently, like the last one he will ever get to make a film for.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A simple story told with unrelenting force, The Northman soars thanks to its staggering visuals, thundering score and with iconic central performance.
reviews.author: Luke Walpole

reviews.text: What Eggers has delivered is a relatively epic and unsurprisingly ambitious exercise thats loaded with some tremendous imagery, his trademark detail, and grisly violence, yet somehow feels unduly restrained.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: A revenge thriller with an elevated horror heart and an anthropologists eye for detail and ritual. But despite the layered imagination that went into recreating this ancient world, it is still the most conventional film yet from Eggers.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Eggers’ immersive approach and stylistic flair creates one wild, applause-worthy combat scene after another, reminding viewers why he’s one of the most unique visual artists working today.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: For the most part it’s an enthralling immersion in a forbidding time and place, enhanced by an immoderately attractive cast and saddled only by a dramatic sameness that settles in after a while and gradually diminishes the film’s impact.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: while the films craft is exemplary and its drama brutal, "The Northman" is not as memorable a film as Eggers prior two.  This critic recalls Nicolas Winding Refn's 2009 "Valhalla Rising" more fondly.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The Northman delivers a brutal and Shakespearean epic, continuing to prove Robert Eggers is one of the best directors in the business.
reviews.author: Caitlin Chappell

reviews.text: The Northman is the kind of movie that breaks down that revenge-driven narrative and weaves it into a story of a lost boy trying to find answers only to be confronted with a different reality than he wanted to believe.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Its revenge-odyssey narrative operates along such a primal wavelength one could easily imagine Eggers discovering it inscribed on a cave wall.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: The Northman, is a grim masterwork of guttural vengeance.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: The most metal adaptation of 'Hamlet' you're ever likely to see.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: The Northman is epic, hypnotising and compelling.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Beneath the runes and visions, it's a tale as old as Game of Thrones, and as simple as a story told around a campfire: a ride of the Valkyries spelled out in gore and popcorn.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: This is intimate, culturally rich storytelling on a brutally epic scale.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: Eggers continues to cement himself among the greats with a fierce Viking tale of vengeance. It's a good mix of visual thunder and blood-soaked violence. Skarsgard's tank-like stature drives the narrative beautifully. Kidman surprises....big time.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: The Northman is raw, savage and uncompromising. It's a ruthless revenge story set during the Viking Age, and Alexander Skarsgård is a beast of a man.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: A brutal revenge tale that straddles the line between arthouse and mainstream entertainment.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: You can almost taste the sweat and the salt and and the fire, grounding the experience in the tangible, but hovering just on the edge of every frame is the sense that there might be something greater at work.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: The Northman can't help but feel like a wild stallion being reluctantly reined in. For all its screaming and grunting, the film is subdued; a retold revenge story with strong pillars but no inner life.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: Eggers' deep dive into VikingNorse culture and religion is fascinating. However, an unsatisfying and routine tale of murder and revenge that surprises no one is only saved by the Hannibal-esque moments of violence.
reviews.author: Andrew Mack

reviews.text: Eggers's execution feels hollow, capturing the horror but undercutting the heart. So in the end, the blows  while intense and gory  don't hit as hard as I'd have hoped.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A delightfully offbeat epic. No guts, no glory!
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: A truly distinctive epic, blending brutal violence, powerhouse performances and otherworldly imagery into its volcanic rampage of revenge. Unmissable.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: The movie has much to recommend it — a powerful cast, certainly, and a different sort of performance from Nicole Kidman, among other things — but it’s a lot.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Not a movie for those who dont consider themselves at least slightly adventurous and open-minded.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: A few centuries of exposure to the formal theatrical tragedies have prepared us for the storys inevitable narrative arcs. But the richness of Eggerss historical ventriloquism ensures there is never a dull moment.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The Northman is an exhilarating, unrelenting, authentically barbaric tale of rage and romance with the performance of a lifetime from Alexander Skarsgård
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Eggers stages much of it in painterly fashion, including a battle royale set in a flaming landscape that captures both the raw power of nature and the barbaric fury of the men fighting in its lap.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: A hulking, bloody Skarsgard makes quite an engrossing action hero. He performs some physical feats in single takes that either are impressively practiced or seamlessly enhanced with visual effects. That you can't tell which makes the action compelling.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Eggers brand of psychological shock is bolder here than his prior works and potent in bursts, but barely works on boldness alone.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Theres mild satisfaction to be found in some of the destructive confrontations, but plenty of dawdling via bewildering rites and rituals that eat up screentime, sapping opportunities for more thrilling Viking exploits.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Genuinely thrilling from start to finish.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Robert Eggers blood-soaked Viking epic isnt just the film of the year so far  its a widescreen rallying cry for cinema in the age of streaming
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: The Northman is a brooding, fierce revenge flick and a bold, modern epic made by a unique visionary storyteller that simultaneously challenges and entertains.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: The best kind of multi-quadrant movie: Without abandoning his arthouse credentials, Eggers has made a rousingly rough, extreme action saga that has the potential of attracting the kind of viewers who might have found his previous work impenetrable.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Rumours of recuts and difficult testing haven’t reduced its essence: like Skarsgård’s brawny frame, it stands more than tall enough at 137 minutes. It comes at you with whopping set-pieces and a ragged, reckless sense of structure.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: It feels compromised, but the great stuff outweighs the not-so-great stuff. To see or not to see? If that is the question, the answer is: see it.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: A one-note fiasco and a foam-flecked depiction of cartoon machismo from a gifted film-maker who should have known better.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It’s ultimately rather dull and hardly any fun...
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: An incredible achievement, amplifying a blood-soaked adventure epic in the haunting specters of witchcraft and folklore that will still challenge viewers without leaving them fully out in the cold.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: The Northman is a feast of visuals and balanced storytelling. It considers Norse storytelling and history that shows Eggers' prowess as both a director and a writer.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Eggers fans, and the cinematically curious, who will come away dazed, and sometimes dazzled.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: With The Northman, we encounter the brilliant execution of a fairly demented vision. To see it is to think, simultaneously, “Wow” and “What were they thinking?!”
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: All hail an egg-head whose non-macho masterpiece is hopefully about to set the world on fire.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A work of bold imagination, not another offshoot of a familiar IP. That alone deserves respect.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Uncompromisingly grim and savage.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: I call upon Odin: may The Northman make a billion dollars.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: In a movie era that’s been defined by compromise, The Northman rides into theaters with the fury of a valkyrie — it’s the rare studio epic that would sooner die than submit to modern precepts of how it should be told.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Although the film ends up as a shallow rumination on revenge and single-minded dominance, it’s hard to beat as spectacle. In terms of making history exciting and engrossing, The Northman is about as titillating as gateway drugs get.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The definitive Viking epic, The Northman is a brilliant melding of arthouse and blockbuster. A stone-cold masterpiece.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: With a strong sense of authenticity and purpose, The Northman is designed to unnerve and repel. In a wide release landscape of easy-to-please, vaporous entertainment, such feats should be celebrated.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: It’s entirely outrageous, with some epic visions of the flaring cosmos. I couldn’t look away.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The Northman is a mystical waking nightmare of drama, adventure, and horror that combine into something truly dark, bewitching, and visceral.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: There are few filmmakers that can make the leap from smaller, insular stories into large-scale epics, but with The Northman, Eggers has proved that his style and substance can remain intact, regardless of the size of the story.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: Robert Eggers manages to deliver a nightmarish epic of blood and busted skulls, fully making good on its premise, but stumbles when it attempts to deviate too far from its core concept.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: Robert Eggers spins a brutal Viking epic with a dash of eerie Shakespearean tragedy.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: Performance, setting, look, and sound come together to create an engaging fantasy that will wow. With meticulously choreographed fight sequences and a distinct aesthetic, The Northman succeeds where other stories like 2007's Beowulf and 2006's 300 fail.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: The film has a lot going for it, fantastic battle scenes & mysticism that elevates the protagonist's journey, but it is lacking in overall character.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Your jaw is so often left gaping in awe from its stunning cinematography and in terror from its ferocity to the point you might just resign yourself to keeping it open for the duration of the film.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: The powerful and moving new film by co-writer and director Robert Eggers is a story you've seen before, but you've never seen it like this.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: In making the violent Viking epic The Northman, Robert Eggers has found a way to craft a revenge tale that audiences will go for, while not compromising his style.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: A staggering feat of visceral filmmaking, The Northman, like Eggers' previous films, warrants profound analysis while still delivering a high-octane action odyssey.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: While the canvas of Robert Eggers latest is considerably broader than that of The Witch and the Lighthouse, it feels as if its psychological chaos hasn't expanded accordingly.
reviews.author: Mark Hanson

reviews.text: Robert Eggers delivers big yet again. The entire ensemble sizzles in this ferocious revenge tale that envelopes you in the 10th Century and ensures you feel every ounce of the story's passion and aggression via the expertly crafted camerawork.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

synopsis: The Northman is an epic revenge thriller, that explores how far a Viking prince will go to seek justice for his murdered father.
